hook.title: How to change orbits using the *least fuel* possible

scenes.title: Burn *1*
scenes.caption: speed up: stretch the orbit into an ellipse

scenes.title: *Coast*
scenes.caption: half an orbit out to the high point

scenes.title: Burn *2*
scenes.caption: speed up again: round it out at the new height

scenes.title: That's a *Hohmann* transfer
scenes.caption: Burnline plans it, plus bi-elliptic, plane change and phasing

caption:
The cheapest way between two circular orbits (most of the time) is two burns.

Burn once to stretch your orbit into an ellipse that touches the new height. Coast half an orbit. Burn again at the top to make it circular.

That's a Hohmann transfer, from 1925, and it's still how it's done. Burnline's planner does Hohmann, bi-elliptic, plane changes and phasing, and every delta-v is checked against the textbook's printed numbers.

Want the bi-elliptic one next? It beats Hohmann in one specific case.
